modelResponse.rhythm: Sinus Rhythm with diffuse ST elevation
keyECGEvidence: Diffuse concave (upward-scooping) ST elevation 1-2 mm in leads I, II, aVL, aVF, V3-V6
PR-segment depression in leads II, III, aVF, V4-V6
NO reciprocal ST depression in any other lead
modelResponse.mechanism: Inflammation of the pericardium causing diffuse epicardial injury current, typically following a viral prodrome
contributingFactors: Chest pain sharp, pleuritic, worse supine, improved leaning forward
Pericardial friction rub heard on auscultation

rejectedAlternatives.why: ST elevation is diffuse and concave rather than convex/tombstoning; absence of reciprocal ST depression; troponin T 0.03 ng/mL is only mild HIGH (non-specific) vs critical; pain is pleuritic/positional rather than ischemic; patient is 31 with no cardiac risk factors.
While possible given the URI, the classic PR depression and pericardial friction rub strongly favor primary pericarditis; BNP 45 pg/mL is normal, suggesting no significant ventricular dysfunction.

recommendedActions: Initiate high-dose Aspirin or NSAIDs (e.g., Ibuprofen)
Administer Colchicine to reduce recurrence risk
Avoid anticoagulation unless pulmonary embolism or MI is confirmed
Continue cardiac monitoring for progression to pericardial effusion/tamponade
